title: Principles of Physiotherapy Intervention: Exercise, Manual Therapy and Rehabilitation

items.q: Which of the following best describes Maitland concept?
o: the process of restoring a person to the best possible function after illness
a graded approach to passive joint mobilisation based on patient response
the rule that tissues adapt only when asked to work beyond their usual load
a scale on which the patient gives a symptom a number from zero upward
items.s: Maitland concept: a graded approach to passive joint mobilisation based on patient response. The other options describe Numerical rating scale, Overload principle, Rehabilitation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Passive range of motion?
o: movement produced entirely by the therapist while the patient stays relaxed
deep heating produced by high-frequency electromagnetic energy
the uniform squeezing force water exerts on a submerged body
movement in which the patient moves with some help from the therapist
items.s: Passive range of motion: movement produced entirely by the therapist while the patient stays relaxed. The other options describe Hydrostatic pressure, Shortwave diathermy, Active assisted range of motion.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Shortwave diathermy?
o: exercise in which the far segment of the limb stays fixed
the rule that training effects are limited to the system that was trained
deep heating produced by high-frequency electromagnetic energy
gentle movement applied to a nerve to restore its ability to glide
items.s: Shortwave diathermy: deep heating produced by high-frequency electromagnetic energy. The other options describe Specificity principle, Closed chain exercise, Neural mobilisation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the process of restoring a person to the best possible function after illness”?
o: Community reintegration
Discharge planning
Functional training
Rehabilitation
items.s: Rehabilitation is the process of restoring a person to the best possible function after illness.

items.q: The statement “the process of restoring a person to the best possible function after illness” describes which of the following?
o: Aids and adaptations
Transfer training
Rehabilitation
Multidisciplinary team
items.s: Rehabilitation is the process of restoring a person to the best possible function after illness.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Therapeutic exercise?
o: a group of different professionals who plan and deliver care together
a sequence combining breathing control, expansion and huffing to clear secretions
equipment and changes to the environment that make daily tasks easier
planned bodily movement performed to correct impairment and improve function
items.s: Therapeutic exercise: planned bodily movement performed to correct impairment and improve function. The other options describe Active cycle of breathing, Multidisciplinary team, Aids and adaptations.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Halliwick concept.
o: a contraction in which the muscle lengthens under load while producing force
a water-based approach teaching control of the body through rotation and balance
the smallest change in score that a patient would notice as worthwhile
a pattern of pool exercise in which the therapist fixes and moves the patient
items.s: Halliwick concept: a water-based approach teaching control of the body through rotation and balance. The other options describe Bad Ragaz ring method, Eccentric contraction, Minimal clinically important difference.

items.q: The statement “a water-based approach teaching control of the body through rotation and balance” describes which of the following?

Hydrotherapy
Halliwick concept
Aquatic exercise
items.s: Halliwick concept is a water-based approach teaching control of the body through rotation and balance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Validity?
o: a pattern of pool exercise in which the therapist fixes and moves the patient
the extent to which a tool measures what it is meant to measure
treatment using a focused beam of light energy applied to tissue
a line on which the patient marks the strength of a symptom such as pain
items.s: Validity: the extent to which a tool measures what it is meant to measure. The other options describe Laser therapy, Visual analogue scale, Bad Ragaz ring method.

a graded approach to passive joint mobilisation based on patient response
the upward force of water that reduces the weight borne by the body
items.s: Goal setting: agreeing clear targets with the patient so that treatment has direction. The other options describe Buoyancy, Tapotement, Maitland concept.

items.s: Exercise progression: the planned advance of an exercise in difficulty as the patient improves. The other options describe Visual analogue scale, Aquatic exercise, End feel.

items.s: Diaphragmatic breathing: breathing that emphasises movement of the diaphragm rather than the upper chest. The other options describe Hydrotherapy, Outcome measure, Transfer training.

items.s: Progressive resistance: a method of steadily increasing the load as the muscle grows stronger. The other options describe Accessory movement, Active range of motion, Neural mobilisation.
